headline: Postponed indefinitely the Ward 5 overnight on-street parking ordinance O-26-020; recommended final passage of surplus property sale and tax deeded property auction resolutions.
summary: Presentations from the Parking Department and written comments from Thornton Tomasetti and the City Clerk covered overnight parking in Ward 5. A motion to indefinitely postpone Ordinance O-26-020 carried. Members also recommended final passage of resolutions R-26-046, on selling surplus property, and R-26-051, on auctioning tax deeded property.
decisions: Accepted the communications on R-26-046 from the Director of Public Works and the Planning Manager and placed them on file.
Accepted the communications on the proposed Ward 5 overnight parking legislation and on O-26-020 and placed them on file.
Recommended final passage of R-26-046, authorizing the sale of surplus property. The minutes give no vote count.
Recommended final passage of R-26-051, relative to auctioning tax deeded property. The minutes give no vote count.
Indefinitely postponed O-26-020, allowing overnight on-street parking in Ward 5 from May 1 to October 31 except on certain main roads. The minutes give no vote count.

City of Nashua  July 20, 2026 
 Proposed Ward 5 Overnight Parking 
Legislation 26025794.PR 
Liz Hannum Nashua Parking Management 
 
 
 
At the request of the City of Nashua, Thornton Tomasetti (“TT”) reviewed a proposed amendment 
to the Code of Ordinances, Part II, Chapter 320, Article XII (“Night Parking”.) This proposed 
amendment would authorize ‘overnight parking1’ within Ward 5 between May 1st and October 31st 
with the exception of select streets 2 within the ward. In response to the request to review the 
referenced legislation, TT has the following comments: 
 
1. Nowhere in the current Code of Ordinances in effect is there a listing “Private Streets” 
within the City of Nashua or Ward 5. This listing should be part of the Code of Ordinances 
to define those areas where codes pertaining to the use of public streets are not germane, 
especially within Ward 5 where there is a significant concentration of private roadways. 
This should be addressed prior to passage of the proposed amendment.  
2. Nowhere in the current Code of Ordinances is stated that, in alignment with New 
Hampshire Revised Statutes § 262:32, any “…vehicle has been left unattended on any 
way or the right-of-way thereof for a period of greater than 24 hours” may be subject for 
removal and impoundment. This should be addressed prior to passage of the proposed 
amendment.  
3. The language as proposed does not reference the terms and conditions noted under § 
320-78.1 (“Overnight on-street parking program in designated downtown areas”) as 
germane to this amendment. As a result, the amendment could be read as authorizing 
any “…operator of any vehicle to park…” on any public street within Ward 5 between May 
1st and October 31 st with the exclusion of those streets named. This runs counter to 
existing ordinances which limit overnight parking on public streets within Nashua to 
qualifying permit holders as detailed in § 320-78.1. This should be addressed prior to 
passage of the proposed amendment.  
4. The language also creates potential conflicts with § 320-73 (“Parking of tractor-trailer-
trucks on certain streets”), § 320-77 (“Unregistered vehicles”), and § 320-77.2 (“Campers 
and recreational vehicles”) with the stipulation of “any vehicle” other those covered by 
 
1 Per § 320-78 (Parking time limits) of the Nashua Code of Ordinances: “Except as hereinafter provided, it shall be 
unlawful for an operator of any vehicle to park the vehicle for a period longer than two hours between 12:00 midnight 
and 6:00 a.m., daily, on any public way in the City where overnight on-street permit parking is not allowed. It shall be 
unlawful for an operator of any vehicle to park the vehicle for any time period between the hours of 12:00 midnight and 
6:00 a.m., daily, without a permit on the public ways where overnight on-street permit parking is allowed.” 
 
2 Buckmeadow Road, Conant Road, Depot Road, Gilson Road, Groton Road, Main Dunstable Road, and West Hollis 
Street.
Re: Proposed Ward 5 Overnight Parking Legislation 
Page 2 
 
 
 
 
 
these existing ordinances. This should be addressed prior to passage of the proposed 
amendment.  
5. Passage of this amendment should also be subject to, and not supersede, § 320-84 
(“Leaving room for traffic”). This is a key ordinance maintaining clear right-of-way to public 
safety and service vehicles and should be addressed prior to passage of the proposed 
amendment.  
6. The document does not include the following potential impacts which should be included 
within the “Fiscal Note” section, including, but not limited to: 
a. The cost to install regulatory signage on all Ward 5 public roadways authorized 
to support overnight parking, indicating the practice is allowed in those areas 
during the prescribed dates. 
b. The labor associated with registering permit holders within Ward 5. 
c. The materials costs associated with registering permit holders within Ward 5. 
d. The incremental increased labor costs associated with dispatching parking 
enforcement personnel through Ward 5 more than one per day to monitor 
compliance with the amendment.  
e. The incremental increased labor costs associated with processing parking 
citations for individuals violating the terms of the amendment. 
f. The incremental increased labor costs associated with adjudicating appealed 
parking citations for individuals ticketed for violating the terms of the amendment. 
g. The anticipated increased revenues arising from successful collection of permit 
registration fees and valid citations issued in violation of the amendment. 
7. The proposed amendment does not appear to include any reference to or input from the 
Police Department, Fire Department, and the Department of Public Works with regards 
to practical impacts from allowing large scale overnight parking along public streets within 
Ward 5. Before the amendment can be passed, it would seem appropriate to request all 
these agencies review the proposed changes and indicate whether critical services such 
as high-speed emergency response, trash pick-up, street sweeping, etc. might be 
adversely impacted and, if so, to what extent.

Date: July 20, 2026 
 
Subject: O-26-020 – Allowing Overnight On-Street Parking in Ward 5 from May 1 through October 31, Except 
on Certain Main Roads 
 
To: Alderman Michael B. O'Brien Sr., Chair, and Members of the Committee on Infrastructure 
 
I am writing to provide the Committee with additional information regarding O-26-020, which proposes 
allowing overnight on-street parking in Ward 5. 
 
I would like the Committee to be aware that, following each decennial U.S. Census, ward boundaries may be 
adjusted through the redistricting process. As a result, some addresses may be reassigned to a different ward. 
Additionally, there are many streets where one side is located in one ward while the opposite side is located in 
another. 
 
As the office responsible for administering elections across all nine wards, the City Clerk's Office regularly 
assists residents who are unsure which ward their address is located in. Although ward information is available 
on the City's website, many residents are not aware of their ward designation. 
 
As written, an ordinance that applies only to Ward 5 may create confusion for residents attempting to determine 
whether overnight parking is permitted at their address. 
 
Thank you for your consideration. 
 
Respectfully, 
 
 
 
Daniel Healey 
Nashua City Clerk
